notes: Curriculum and optional references checked against OEE commit 67416343f3eab17ada5d3c79ae6cc782524c29ff on 2026-11-20. Nand to Tetris project numbers are verified official resources but use a different 16-bit Hack architecture; OEE SEF1 requires its own 8-bit teaching model and distinct public assessments. Chapter numbers refer only to The Elements of Computing Systems, second edition (2021, ISBN 9780262539807). No external project, book, purchase, or tool substitutes for OEE assessment evidence. The maintainer reviewed this source-pinned resource map and its documented gaps on 2026-11-20. Reviewed status approves the resource recommendations as qualified here; it does not upgrade partial modules to mapped, establish educational course readiness, or replace OEE assessment evidence.

modules.title: Bits and Representation
modules.gap: Confirmed sections introduce binary values and character encodings but do not independently cover OEE's address-versus-value distinction, historical switching devices or physical voltage/noise assumptions. Follow the canonical course for those topics.

resources.purpose: Use the free interactive explanations to compare bit patterns, binary/decimal/hexadecimal values and character encodings; distinguish a byte pattern from its interpretation.
Official free Boolean Logic project supplies NAND-based gate building and truth-table checks; adapt the examples to OEE's own gate criteria instead of submitting this external project as evidence.
Optional second-edition Boolean Logic chapter, if legally available; not necessary to complete the free project or OEE module.

modules.title: Registers and Memory
modules.gap: Official project uses Hack's 16-bit registers and large RAM hierarchy, not OEE's four-cell eight-bit store. Its sequential-logic work does not independently teach OEE's bus contention, clock-edge and reset convention checks. Adapt explicitly.

resources.purpose: Free Memory project covers clocked state, enabled writes, registers and addressable RAM; compare its architecture against the OEE eight-bit model.
Optional second-edition Memory chapter for register and address-selection theory; use OEE for the assessed four-cell semantics.

modules.title: Arithmetic and ALU
modules.gap: Official materials implement the 16-bit Hack adders/ALU, not OEE's eight-bit carry chain, modulo-256 behavior and selected-result zero detector. These OEE-specific checks remain to be practiced independently.

resources.purpose: Free Boolean Arithmetic project supplies half/full adder and ALU construction examples; reason explicitly about width and zero detection differences.
Optional second-edition Boolean Arithmetic chapter; derive the OEE eight-bit oracle independently rather than copying the Hack ALU.

modules.title: Processor Execution
modules.gap: Project 5 uses a different Hack datapath and instruction encoding. It does not establish the OEE two-byte fetch, atomic state commit or fault-state semantics. Use the canonical OEE machine for those investigations.

resources.purpose: Free Computer Architecture project illustrates how CPU, ALU and memory connect; inspect differences from OEE's reference machine.
Optional second-edition Computer Architecture chapter for broader processor and memory organization.

modules.title: Instructions and Programs
modules.gap: Project 4 uses Hack assembly and machine language, not OEE's two-byte aligned opcodes, ADDI/ANDI, conditional JZ or illegal-address behavior. Do not reuse Hack branch traces as OEE answers.

resources.purpose: Free Machine Language project shows instruction encoding and low-level program tracing in a separate architecture.
Optional second-edition Machine Language chapter for instruction/data distinctions and example machine programs.

modules.title: Devices and Boot
modules.gap: Computer Architecture project demonstrates memory-mapped screen/keyboard but does not explain OEE's firmware, bootloader, persistent storage/file-system boundary or polling-versus-interrupt distinctions. Those require additional independent sources.

resources.purpose: Inspect the free project's memory-mapped I/O design as an alternative architecture; verify OEE's device-latch behavior from its own specification.
Optional context for the Hack memory-mapped device interface; not an explanation of real boot or operating-system startup.

modules.title: Computer System Integration
modules.gap: Project 5 integrates Hack's 16-bit components, not the OEE eight-bit program-to-output trace or its required fault injection, assumptions and limitations defense. OEE's final integration evidence must use the canonical model.

resources.purpose: Use the free complete Hack computer project as a comparative system-level integration exercise, not a substitute for the OEE program-to-output investigation.
Optional second-edition architecture overview to compare with OEE's integrated reference machine.
